.
Be sure to know your precinct before arriving at the polls
click here
There are poll workers who will be able to help you find your precinct.
Voting in Marshfield
All precincts vote at Marshfield High School Gymnasium, 167 Forest St.  Enter behind the Ram statue.  There are people in the lobby to help you find your precinct if you need help, otherwise enter the gym and go directly to your precinct.
In the Gym, at the check-In table tell the poll worker the first three letters of your last name, followed by the first three letters of your first name, then announce your full name, your street number and street name.  The Poll worker will repeat the information back to you.  The poll worker will give you a ballot.
If your name does not appear on the list the poll worker will send you to the Precinct Warden's table.  If the Warden cannot resolve the issue you may be required to vote provisionally so that we can determine why you are not on our list.  An example would be a college student who registered at school, graduated and forgot to change their voter registration back to Marshfield.
To cast your vote, follow the voting instructions in the voting booth by filling in the oval directly across from the name you wish to vote. If you need assistance, you may bring someone to assist you or ask a poll worker to provide confidential, non-partisan help.  If you make a mistake - ask the Warden or Clerk at the Table at the rear of your Precinct for a replacement ballot.  You are permitted up to three ballots.  If you err on the third ballot, the Warden or Clerk can advise you how to best handle your mistake so that your choice will be correctly tallied even if the machine is unable to read your ballot electronically.
NO political paraphernalia may be displayed within 150 feet of the entrance to the polling location (includes signs, stickers, clothing and lapel buttons).  If you have a cheat sheet for answering the questions or filling out your ballots that paper must be held in such a way as to not be visible to other voters.  Please make sure you remove any paper you bring into the voting booth area - pretend you are camping.
Voting Absentee
Link to Absentee Ballot Application
Application for absentee ballots may be submitted in-person at the Town Clerk's Office, by mail or email. If a voter submits the application in-person he may obtain the ballot and vote in person over-the -counter. Otherwise, the ballot is sent by mail.  No person may leave the Town Hall with a ballot in hand.  If a family member is hospitalized within 48 hours of an election special arrangements can be made, please speak directly to the Town Clerk who can be found either at the Clerk's Office prior to Election Day at the High School on Election Day walking hither and yon putting out small fires.
Members of the same household may request absentee ballots for their housemates and must be 18 years of age.
If there is a hospitalization in your family within one week of the election, please contact the Town Clerk's Office and we will make arrangements for you to carry a ballot to your loved one so that they can vote absentee.
